recent_posts.text: How to prevent budget overruns in an organization, and what cyber-risks the value of AI tokens creates. Not long ago, many companies began actively implementing AI agents in a wide variety of workflows. Very quickly, the cost of using them became a pressing issue for companies. Moreover, it’s an issue that concerns more than just finance department — in addition to budgetary concerns, issues of reliability, operational stability, and even information security have emerged. This is because the cost of automating one and the same process varies significantly from one deployment to the next, is unpredictable, and could be subject to external influences. Furthermore, for a malicious actor attacking an organization, any process automated using AI and vulnerable to external influence is, in essence, a convenient target for a “new type of DDoS attack”. Application-error reports, product reviews, or technical support requests can (just like any other external data that a company processes via AI) serve as a tool in an attack aimed at increasing consumption of tokens (word fragments that serve as the basic unit of input and output of an LLM). recent_posts.title: Grindr users’ sensitive data shared through ad auctions without valid consent
recent_posts.text: Advertising company Xandr has been fined $9.6 million over data sharing that could reveal Grindr users’ sexual orientation. Norway’s privacy regulator Datatilsynet has fined advertising technology company Xandr 92 million Norwegian kroner, approximately $9.6 million, for unlawfully processing and sharing sensitive information about Grindr users. While the decision concerns users in Norway, the data-sharing practices were not confined to Norwegian users. BleepingComputer reports that information about Grindr users in other countries was also exposed through the advertising system. Between July 2018 and April 2020, Xandr handled real-time advertising auctions involving Grindr users. These automated auctions let advertisers bid to display an ad, but also involved circulating information about the person who would see it. Sensitive information revealing sexual orientation could potentially reach thousands of companies. Crucially, users did not have to disclose their sexual orientation in their profiles. recent_posts.title: TAG-217 Targets South Korean Financial Services with ARTEX
recent_posts.text: Learn how threat actor TAG-217 used the AI-driven ARTEX framework to target South Korean financial institutions in recent cyberattacks. The threat actor linked to recent AI-assisted attacks on South Korean financial institutions was testing infrastructure and assembling attack tools as early as August 2026, weeks before the banking campaign became public, according to new research from Recorded Future’s Insikt Group. Subsequent public reporting indicated that the breaches exposed personal data belonging to at least 68,000 people across at least seven financial institutions. Insikt Group’s investigation expands the known timeline and capabilities of the actor, tracked as TAG-217. Insikt Group uncovered tools designed to steal cryptocurrency wallet files, gain greater access to Linux systems, and test weaknesses in mobile devices. The findings illustrate the “ jagged edge ” of AI-enabled attacks: threat actors realizing significant gains while committing basic operational security mistakes. recent_posts.title: Training AIs to Solve CAPTCHAs
recent_posts.text: Interesting research : Abstract : Vision-language models (VLMs) can solve visual CAPTCHAs without task-specific training, but the agents built on them approach every challenge from scratch. For such an agent, the hundredth instance of a familiar puzzle costs as much time and compute as the first. Specialized detectors invert the trade-off, answering in milliseconds but only for categories they were trained on. Neither improves with exposure. We study what changes when a solver improves with use. Our system pairs a fine-tuned YOLOv8 detector with an open-weight VLM behind a confidence-based router, and runs entirely from screenshots and operating-system input events, with no browser automation or DOM access. It reaches 85.4% overall and 84.2% macro accuracy across 16 classes, exceeding either component alone. Every answer VLM produces also serves as a training label, so the detector absorbs categories it was never trained for, typically after one or two encounters and without human annotation. At home in Michigan, Jordan was readying for a weekend trip when he received a friend request on Instagram. The invite was sent by a user named “dani.robertts” whose profile showed an attractive young woman. After accepting the request, Jordan and the account chatted about nothing in particular—teenage matters, getting to know one another—before “dani” became flirtatious, eventually sending Jordan what she claimed was a nude photograph of herself. Jordan responded in kind with an explicit photograph of himself. But here, a trap was revealed. “Dani Robertts” was not a young, friendly, interested woman. Dani Robertts was several men, sending messages from thousands of miles away in Lagos, Nigeria, who had followed a script to pressure young men into handing over their money. recent_posts.title: Highlights of Microsoft’s October Patch Release | Kaspersky official blog
recent_posts.text: The update collection published by Microsoft on October 13, 2026 includes a total of 1,414 patches. Here’s what you need to know. Microsoft’s October Patch Tuesday update stands out for two reasons. First, the total number of patches has reached four digits for the first time. Second, to help companies better understand the details of the vulnerabilities, Microsoft has decided to group them into risk cohorts . A cohort brings together vulnerabilities that are exploited under the same conditions and affect the same systems. They replace neither the severity rating, nor the individual bulletins for each CVE. While they’re unlikely to be suitable for comprehensive patch prioritization , they will help quickly assess which part of an infrastructure is currently most at risk. Statistics corner Of the 1,414 vulnerabilities addressed in the October Patch Tuesday release, 1,102 directly affect the Windows operating system, 134 — Microsoft Office, 36 — SharePoint Server, 22 — SQL Server, and seven — Exchange Server. recent_posts.title: Man seeking love travels 2,000 km to meet an AI-generated woman
recent_posts.text: An influencer’s invitation to join her on a farm shows how public videos can feel dangerously personal. A 49-year-old bricklayer sold his belongings before traveling 2,000 km by bus from his home in Brazil to meet “Jéssica,” an online influencer he had fallen for. Yet despite having a social media account with more than 300,000 followers, she never existed. Edimar Rocha Martins lives in Imperatriz, a city in northeastern Brazil. He says he struck up an online conversation with Jéssica Fazendeira, who supposedly lived near the southeastern city of Belo Horizonte. The AI persona promising love The online persona’s name, “Fazendeira,” loosely translates as “female farmer.” She described herself as living on a farm. Martins said that he had been talking with the persona online since 2020. He decided to visit her after she offered to pay for his trip and have him live on the farm with her, he said. The account’s operator disputes this, saying the character was created in 2025 and denying any private messages with him. recent_posts.text: Learn how to write a resume with AI, protect your personal data, and improve your chances of catching a recruiter’s attention — with practical tips and a ready-made prompt. Finding a job these days is playing on hard mode. You send your resume to a company, and a couple of minutes later, an automated rejection lands in your inbox. And then it happens again. And again. Sound familiar? In this post, we look at how recruiting platforms work from the HR side. We also show how to use AI safely as a copy editor so you can prepare a resume for recruiters without turning it into a lifeless pile of keywords. At the end, we share a ready-made prompt to help you improve your resume’s structure and content. Protecting your data Before you give your resume to a chatbot, remove all sensitive information: your name, phone number, home address, email, company names, and scans of documents. Any language model you chat with can sometimes memorize personal information contained in their training data. recent_posts.title: Backdooring Open-Weight AI Models
recent_posts.text: This is a problem: Any open model whose weights have been edited can carry a backdoor, whether it’s a task-specific fine-tune, a merged adapter or an abliterated build. We have abliterated models in the title because it’s the most popular reason people download modified weights without verifying what’s inside. Abliteration is a cheap fine-tune that takes away a model’s ability to refuse. You find the direction in the weights that carries “no” and subtract it. The model then answers things a safety-tuned version would turn down. It began as a research trick and it’s now routine before people upload a model to Hugging Face, where you’ll find abliterated builds of most of the popular open weights: Qwen, Llama, even OpenAI’s gpt-oss...
